name: SIN
description: SIN returns the sine of a given angle. The angle must be expressed in radians.
tldr: Returns the sine of an angle given in radians.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The angle, in radians, for which you want the sine.

basicExample.explanation: RADIANS(30) converts to π/6; the sine of π/6 is 0.5.

advancedExamples.title: Sine of π/2
advancedExamples.explanation: The sine of π/2 radians (90°) is 1.

howItWorks: SIN computes the sine of an angle measured in radians. The function is periodic with period 2π, so SIN(x) = SIN(x + 2πk) for any integer k.

howToSteps.name: Convert if needed
howToSteps.text: If your angle is in degrees, wrap it with RADIANS().

howToSteps.name: Enter the formula
howToSteps.text: Type =SIN(number) with the angle in radians.

limitations: The angle must be in radians; degrees must be converted with RADIANS or PI()/180.
Results are approximate due to floating-point math.

commonErrors.cause: Angle supplied in degrees instead of radians.
commonErrors.fix: Wrap the angle in RADIANS() or multiply by PI()/180.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: SIN works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: My SIN gives wrong values — why?
faq.answer: Most likely you passed degrees. Convert with RADIANS() first, e.g. =SIN(RADIANS(30)).

faq.question: What is the period of SIN?
How do I get the inverse (angle from sine)?
faq.answer: Use ASIN, which returns the angle in radians.
